state.goal: A paused broker resumes with PermitAuthority(ledger, max_cumulative_usd=0.8). The ledger hash chain verifies. What is cumulative_cost_usd after replay, and is the next permit issued or refused?

recent_accepted.summary:
Replay sums only numeric, finite, non-negative cost_usd values: 0.25 + 0.5 = 0.75. The null receipt contributes nothing, and the string "0.1" fails the `type(cost) in (int, float)` test, so it is silently skipped. Since 0.75 < 0.8, the cumulative cap check in `issue` does not trip and the next permit is issued.

Caveat worth flagging: real spend was 0.85, which exceeds the cap. The hand-edited string receipt is invisible to replay even though `receipt()` would have rejected it as `invalid_receipt_cost`, and the verifying hash chain gives no signal because the edit was re-chained.

data.summary: Replay yields cumulative_cost_usd = 0.75 (0.25 + 0.5); the string "0.1" and the null are skipped, so 0.75 < 0.8 and the next permit is ISSUED — though true spend is 0.85, over cap.
claims: Replay adds a receipt's cost only when type(cost) is int/float, finite, and >= 0 (code).
cost_usd null (p-2) is skipped: it fails the type check in the replay branch (ledger, code).
cost_usd "0.1" (p-3) is a string, so type(cost) in (int, float) is False and it is silently skipped with no error during replay (ledger, code).
issue() refuses only when _cumulative_cost_usd >= max_cumulative_usd; 0.75 >= 0.8 is False, so the next permit is issued (code, request).
Real spend is 0.25 + 0.1 + 0.5 = 0.85, exceeding the 0.8 cap; replay under-counts by 0.1 (ledger, note).
The string cost would have been rejected by receipt() as invalid_receipt_cost, so it could not have come from the normal write path, consistent with the hand-edit (code, note).
A verifying hash chain does not detect this: the edit was re-chained, so integrity verification gives no signal of the under-count (note, request).
Assumes the four listed receipts are the only cost-bearing events and that replay starts from zero (ledger).
Assumes the next issue() call passes all other checks (ttl, scope, per-permit budget), which are elided in the excerpt (code).
